prediction.likelyOutcome: ASARCO should prevail on Atlantic Richfield's underlying PRP liability and on the (already-resolved) statute of limitations defense, but the bench trial will turn on two compounding, genuinely contested issues: how much of the $111.4 million settlement counts as 'incurred' recoverable response cost (plausibly $61.4M-$111.4M), and what percentage of that base is equitably allocable to Atlantic Richfield (ASARCO's own expert caps this at 25%-41%). The likely net recovery for ASARCO is a fraction of the headline settlement figure, concentrated in roughly the low-to-mid eight figures.

outcome.description: After an eight-day bench trial the district court found ASARCO had incurred $111,403,743 in necessary response costs (the full consent-decree payment) and held Atlantic Richfield liable for 25 percent of them, $27,850,936, adopting the most conservative of ASARCO's expert's allocation strategies (25 to 41 percent) and rejecting Atlantic Richfield's zero allocation; it added a separate $1 million award for Atlantic Richfield's non-cooperation and misrepresentations, so the stated awards total $28,850,936. The Ninth Circuit affirmed the 25 percent allocation (and the unchallenged $1 million award) but vacated the finding that the whole $111.4 million was recoverable now, because about $50 million of trust funds had not been and might never be spent, and remanded to determine which costs were actually incurred. Atlantic Richfield had argued recoverable costs should be limited to about $61.4 million.
outcome.finalNote: Allocation affirmed; cost base vacated and remanded, so no final figure (25 percent of the remand cost base plus the $1 million award).
